reconcile.note: Gill folds the two rubrics into one, reading John 5:29's 'those who have done good' as those who believe in Christ, making works and faith the same underlying criterion.

discrepancy.note: Ingersoll names belief itself as the objection, contrasting John's faith-based salvation scheme with Gospels that never make believing a condition.

quotes.text: One great objection to the New Testament is that it bases salvation upon belief. … It says not one word as to the necessity of believing on Jesus Christ, not one word as to the atonement, not one word upon the scheme of salvation, and not the slightest hint that it is necessary to believe anything here in order to be happy hereafter.
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), The Christian Religion, pt. III (Rejoinder to Judge Black) (1881), on John 3:18 and John 5:29.

sides.snippet: He who believes in him is not judged. He who doesn't believe has been judged already, because he has not believed in the name of the one and only Son of God.
sides.verseText: He who believes in him is not judged. He who doesn't believe has been judged already, because he has not believed in the name of the one and only Son of God.

sides.snippet: those who have done good, to the resurrection of life; and those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgment.
sides.verseText: and will come out; those who have done good, to the resurrection of life; and those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgment.
